---
title: "Reports and exported tables (page 5)"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_prepare.R")
tr <- tut$to_report
best <- tr[["best normalization"]]
conc_file <- grep("\\.conc\\.xlsx$", tut$table_files, value = TRUE)[1]
```

Page 5 of the app, **Report export**, gives you the results to keep: two reports and the tables
of the data. Everything on this page uses one **final normalization method**.

## Final normalization method

Choose the method first; the buttons stay greyed out until you do. **Best** is the method with the
lowest median RSD% among the QC replicates (here `r tut$method_labels[[best]]`), and each option shows
its median RSD%:

```{r}
#| label: table-final-norm
rsd <- tr[["median RSD% per normalization"]]
tut_table(tibble::tibble(Option = c(paste("Best:", tut$method_labels[[best]]), unname(tut$method_labels[names(rsd)])),
                         `Median RSD%` = round(c(rsd[[best]], unname(rsd)), 1)), height = "240px")
```

Choose another method when, for example, 3.8 shows that it works clearly better for the compounds
you are most interested in.

## Reports

| Button | Report | For |
|---|---|---|
| **QC/QA report (html)** | the internal report: all quality-control steps, tables and interactive figures, as on pages 2–4 of the app | checking and documenting the processing |
| **Summary report (pdf)** | the external report: the project, the methods and the results in a few pages | sharing the results |

A progress bar shows how far the report is; the HTML report is shown in the app when it is ready,
and **Download HTML Report** saves it. The reports name the settings that were used, so they
document the processing.

## Exported tables

**Export data into tables** writes four Excel files for the final method (and each of their sheets
as a `.csv` file), ready to download:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `….norm.xlsx` | normalized peak areas of all features (also non-targeted) |
| `….norm_blk.xlsx` | the same after blank subtraction |
| `….conc.xlsx` | concentrations of the targeted compounds: QCs, study samples and blanks |
| `….conc_all.xlsx` | the same with all samples, including the calibration samples |

This is the start of a batch sheet of the concentration table of the example
(`r basename(conc_file)`), the feature columns first and then the samples:

```{r}
#| label: table-export
sh <- openxlsx::getSheetNames(conc_file)
x <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(conc_file, sheet = sh[2], colNames = FALSE, rows = 1:40)
hdr <- which(apply(x, 1, \(r) any(r %in% "Alignment ID")))[1]
cols <- c(which(x[hdr, ] %in% c("Chemical", "LOD", "LLOQ", "ULOQ", "Min Conc.", "Max Conc.", "Avg. Conc.",
                                "Median Conc.", "R2", "Model", "Calibration", "Notes")),
          which(!is.na(x[hdr, ]))[seq(ncol(x) - 3, ncol(x))])
cols <- unique(cols[cols <= ncol(x)])
body <- x[(hdr + 1):nrow(x), cols]
names(body) <- make.unique(as.character(unlist(x[hdr, cols])))
tut_table(utils::head(body[!is.na(body$Chemical), ], 25), height = "380px")
```

**How to read it**

- **Sheets**: *Full* has one row per compound over all batches (average and median of the measured
  values, the curve used per batch); then one sheet per batch with its limits, statistics, model
  and **Notes**, the full text of the note icons of table 4.2.
- **Statistics** (minimum, maximum, average, median) use the measured values of the study samples
  only: values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules are left out.
- **Coloured cells** in the sample columns are values that were replaced or are above the ULOQ;
  the last sheet, *Legend*, explains the colours:

```{r}
#| label: table-legend
leg <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(conc_file, sheet = "Legend", colNames = TRUE)
fills <- c("#FAAFAF", "#FCEACF", "#D3EBF2", "#E3E0B8", "#A8A05A")   # The fills of the exported cells
leg <- leg[!is.na(leg$Meaning) & nzchar(leg$Meaning), "Meaning", drop = FALSE][seq_along(fills), , drop = FALSE]
leg$Colour <- ""
DT::datatable(leg[, c("Colour", "Meaning")], rownames = FALSE, selection = "none",
              options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE, ordering = FALSE)) |>
  DT::formatStyle("Colour", backgroundColor = DT::styleRow(seq_along(fills), fills))
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reuse the processing
Save the settings with **Download settings (.yml)** on page 1. Loading the file later, in the app or
with `run_quanta.R` on the command line, processes new data the same way.
:::
